meta.note: Magnitudes are structural: water balance, land-cover arithmetic and published policy. None is fitted. `tier: corroborated` means an independent regression agrees on the SIGN, not that it set the value.

region_acres.source: dissolved eight-county TIGER boundary, EPSG:5070, via scripts/phase1/region.py

irrigated_acres.source: 2017 Census of Agriculture, Table 10 'Irrigation: 2017 and 2012', USDA NASS Vol 1 Ch 2 Arizona county-level, summed over the eight counties the pipeline selects (Maricopa and Gila in, Graham and La Paz out - PROBLEMS.md P8)

specific_yield.source: Midpoint of the ADWR basin-fill modelling range. USGS SIR 2007-5275 (Pool & Anderson) gives 0.16-0.21 for comparable alluvial aquifers. The exact ADWR value was not retrieved: azwater.gov returns HTTP 403.

alluvial_fraction.source: assumed share of the region that is alluvial basin rather than mountain block

storage_af_per_ft.source: measured at the {horizon['default_scenario_months']}-month scenario horizon by aquifer_calibration.py's spreading-cone sweep: total drawdown over the window regressed on total volume pumped across it, climate and trend controlled, Newey-West. 244,082 AF/ft (t = +1.78), i.e. A_eff = 1,627,214 acres. The band is the plateau across 3-24 month horizons.
storage_af_per_ft.note: Still the dominant uncertainty in Layer 2, but no longer a choice between two assumptions. PHASE3_PLAN.md §12 prescribed the short-run limit (110,891 AF/ft) and the first implementation shipped the long-run one (1,875,168); the sweep measured that the cone spreads but plateaus at two to three times the irrigated area, so the long-run figure is 7.7x past the end of the evidence and the short-run figure understates a 12-month scenario by 2.2x. See §12.

grace_units_per_af.source: 1 AF spread over the region area, in metres of equivalent water height. The GRACE series is lwe_thickness in METRES despite the 'cm' label in the source docstring: its sd is 0.0479, which is 4.8 cm (plausible for a regional anomaly) and not 0.05 mm (not).
grace_units_per_af.note: A closed-basin upper bound: it assumes every acre-foot pumped shows up in the GRACE footprint. The measured irrigation->GRACE slope (-5.222e-08 per AF/month, t = -1.93) is LARGER than this bound, which means it is not a clean structural coefficient — it is used for sign only.

gpcd_groundwater.source: public_supply_groundwater_mgd x 1e6 / population, 2020 means (823.4 MGD / 6,376,433 people)

ndvi_impervious.source: measured: difference-in-differences on MOD13A3 NDVI against NLCD impervious change, 130,833 MODIS cells differenced against themselves (2000-2004 vs 2019-2023). Slope -0.0356 NDVI per unit impervious fraction (HC1 t = -14.7). Cross-sectional fit over 287 months agrees at -0.0250. See scripts/phase3/ndvi_endpoints.py.
ndvi_impervious.note: Stated so that (ndvi_impervious - ndvi_natural) IS the measured slope, because that difference is the whole of what the lever multiplies. The directly measured NDVI of a fully impervious cell is 0.2046; the +0.0143 gap to the value used here is the difference between the regression's zero-impervious intercept (0.2310, the NDVI of the land actually being paved) and ndvi_natural (0.2167, a p50 over months of the whole-region mean). Anchoring on the slope removes that mismatch instead of inheriting it. THE EFFECT IS ALMOST ENTIRELY ABOUT WHAT THE PAVEMENT REPLACED: split by each cell's pre-2005 NDVI, paving dry desert costs -0.0027 (not distinguishable from zero — desert NDVI is already near what pavement reads), while paving cropland or riparian land costs -0.1792, a 45x difference. PHASE3_PARAMS.md §4b's assumed 0.08 endpoint implies -0.1367, which is close to the cropland-conversion case: the assumption was not absurd, it was describing the wrong half of the region. The value adopted here is the historical mix, which is the right one for a slider that adds impervious cover the way this region actually adds it.

ndvi_irrigated_crop.source: measured: difference-in-differences of MOD13A3 NDVI against HUC12 irrigation withdrawal, 126,655 MODIS cells differenced against themselves (2000-2004 vs 2016-2020). Slope +0.3177 NDVI per unit irrigated fraction, baseline-controlled, HC1 t = +33.4 (+0.3356 uncontrolled). See scripts/phase3/ndvi_endpoints.py.
ndvi_irrigated_crop.note: PHASE3_PARAMS.md §4b assumed 0.55 (band 0.45-0.65) and was very nearly right: the measurement is 0.5344, inside the assumed band and 2.8% from its midpoint (0.4% before the irrigated-acres correction of PROBLEMS.md P8; the calibration acres rose 5.5% and the slope fell by the same factor, so the lever irrigated_fraction x slope is unchanged). Stated relative to ndvi_natural so the difference IS the measured slope, as for ndvi_impervious. THE BAND IS NARROW BECAUSE TWO DESIGNS AGREE, NOT BECAUSE THE QUANTITY IS PRECISELY KNOWN: it spans the baseline-controlled and uncontrolled fits, and is deliberately not a confidence interval, since 126,655 MODIS cells are nowhere near independent. There is no cropland mask in the repo, so the predictor is HUC12 withdrawal turned into irrigated area by one calibration on the whole record - coarser than the impervious predictor, and identified off ~339 irrigated HUC12s rather than off fields. The cross-sectional fit is unusable here and visibly so (+0.0486): binned by irrigated fraction, mean NDVI DIPS before it rises, because HUC12s with no irrigation include the mountains while HUC12s with a little are low desert valleys - that fit is measuring elevation.

region_share_of_az_reduction.source: Arizona's shortage reduction is 'borne almost entirely by the CAP system' (ADWR-CAP joint shortage statement, 2021), and CAP delivers only to Maricopa, Pinal and Pima - all three in-region (PROBLEMS.md P8). The residual is 4th-priority on-river water outside the CAP system.
region_share_of_az_reduction.note: Was 0.60 (band 0.40-0.80) on the belief that Maricopa was out-of-region; the region always contained it. Still not a measured number: CAP delivery data by county would replace it.

cfs_per_af_month.source: 1 acre-foot delivered evenly over a mean month, in cubic feet per second

mean_precipitation_mm_day.source: mean of data/Final/precipitation_monthly.csv over the full record

effluent_return_fraction.source: share of municipal supply returned as treated effluent — indoor use reaches the sewer, outdoor use is consumed. The mechanism is primary: 'The Santa Cruz River is largely dependent on discharges from water reclamation facilities' (A Living River: Santa Cruz River 2024, Downtown Tucson to Marana, Supplementary Report, Sonoran Institute).
effluent_return_fraction.note: The fraction itself is a standard water-balance figure, not a cited value.

runoff_coefficient_impervious.source: standard rational-method runoff coefficient for paved surface

runoff_coefficient_natural.source: standard rational-method runoff coefficient for desert soils
runoff_coefficient_natural.note: The same mechanism the Living River report names — 'runoff after storms depends on the amount of impervious surface' — and the reason features.py calls precip_x_impervious the dominant urban-desert discharge term.

stream_capture_fraction.source: share of regional groundwater pumping captured from streamflow rather than from storage. Stream-aquifer depletion is the documented mechanism behind the loss of perennial reach on the Santa Cruz and San Pedro.
stream_capture_fraction.note: Not sourced to a number. Most regional pumping is far from a stream, hence the low central value.

transfer_surface_water_to_wildlife.source: regression of bbs_abundance_anomaly on annual mean discharge_log_anomaly, n = 44 (1980-2024), PDSI-controlled. Riparian corridors carry disproportionate bird abundance in the Southwest.
transfer_surface_water_to_wildlife.note: The trend-controlled (conservative) estimate ships; the band's upper end is the climate-only fit, which is significant (t = +2.19, p = 0.029). The sign is positive in both, unlike Mead, which flipped.

groundwater_substitution_fraction.source: share of lost CAP water replaced by pumping rather than fallowing; Pinal's DCP mitigation explicitly funded new wells

population.source: one person x GPCD, converted to MGD — closes the population -> public supply -> aquifer loop

grace.source: regression of dy on (y_lag1 - ybar), t = -2.28, e-folding 25.9 months

groundwater.note: Not significant. An aquifer barely reverting is physically right, but the rate is weakly identified.

integrate_learned_residual.source: PHASE3_PLAN.md §13 — measured both ways, see the table there
integrate_learned_residual.note: Whether Layer 3 also integrates the LEARNED residual, not just the structural forcing. Off: §4a established the exported models are not dynamical systems, and integrating them amplifies D2's wrong signs (Mead -> NDVI goes from -3.27 to -14.01 score points) without adding any dynamics the models actually contain. The structural layer is integrated either way, because a storage balance really does accumulate.

levers.mechanism: ΔDepth/month = ΔPumping / (S_y · A). More withdrawal, deeper water.
levers.evidence: PHASE3_PLAN.md §12: +9.018e-06 ft per AF/month, t = +3.16, n = 246.

levers.mechanism: Same storage balance; municipal groundwater is pumped from the same aquifer.
levers.evidence: None. PHASE3_PLAN.md §12 finds t = +0.17 / -0.11 / +0.91 across specifications.

levers.mechanism: Δpopulation × per-capita municipal groundwater draw, into the storage balance.
levers.evidence: None. PHASE3_PLAN.md §10 finds 0/5 folds and an effect of -0.113 sd, wrong-signed.

levers.mechanism: Elevation → DCP shortage tier → Arizona reduction (kAF/yr) → in-region share → share replaced by pumping → storage balance. A lower reservoir means more pumping.
levers.evidence: Published law (LBOps Table 1), but no panel support: PHASE3_PLAN.md §12 finds the wrong sign in every specification and t falling to +0.12 under a time control. §10's 5/5-fold agreement was five folds sharing one secular trend.

levers.mechanism: Pumped water leaves the storage GRACE measures, as equivalent water height.
levers.evidence: PHASE3_PLAN.md §12: correct sign in all three specifications, t = -3.61 to -1.93.

levers.mechanism: A lower reservoir substitutes pumping for CAP water, drawing down storage.

Δpopulation × per-capita municipal draw × effluent return fraction → added discharge, as a proportion of total gaged flow. Counterintuitive and correct: the perennial reaches of the Santa Cruz are treated wastewater.
levers.evidence: Mechanism is primary (Living River 2024); the return fraction is assumed.

levers.mechanism: Δimpervious area × (runoff coefficient paved − runoff coefficient desert) × mean precipitation → added storm runoff.
levers.evidence: None from the panel; features.py already treats precip x impervious as the dominant urban-desert discharge term.

levers.mechanism: A share of pumping is captured from streamflow rather than from storage.
levers.evidence: None from the panel. Stream depletion is the documented cause of lost perennial reach on the Santa Cruz and San Pedro.

levers.mechanism: The municipal pumping that population drives is also captured from streams. This runs AGAINST the effluent lever above; the net sign is an output of the model rather than an assumption, and it is positive at the shipped parameters.
A lower reservoir substitutes pumping for CAP water, and part of that pumping is stream capture.
ΔNDVI = (Δimpervious/100) × (NDVI_impervious − NDVI_natural). Pavement is not green.
levers.evidence: Difference-in-differences on the project's own MOD13A3 and NLCD rasters: 130,833 MODIS cells differenced against themselves (2000-2004 vs 2019-2023), slope -0.0356 NDVI per unit impervious fraction, HC1 t = -14.7. A cross-sectional fit over 287 months agrees at -0.0250.

local_effect.headline: On the land actually paved, NDVI falls 16%.
local_effect.detail: The region-wide number is small because the paving is small: the slider's full range is about 2% of the eight counties, and a regional mean is built to average that away. The same coefficient applied to the whole region would be about 40 score points. What the pavement REPLACED is most of the story — paving dry desert costs -0.0027 NDVI, which is not distinguishable from zero because desert is already near what pavement reads, while paving cropland or riparian land costs -0.1792, about 83% of the region's whole vegetation signal.

levers.mechanism: ΔNDVI = Δfraction_of_baseline_withdrawal × irrigated_fraction × (NDVI_crop − NDVI_natural). Positive on irrigated pixels while negative on groundwater — the tension PHASE3_PLAN.md §4 wants shown, not hidden.
levers.evidence: Difference-in-differences on MOD13A3 against HUC12 irrigation withdrawal: 126,655 MODIS cells differenced against themselves (2000-2004 vs 2016-2020), slope +0.3177 NDVI per unit irrigated fraction, HC1 t = +33.4. The dose-response is monotone: cells that LOST irrigation fell below the regional drift, cells that gained rose above it.

transfers.mechanism: Riparian corridors carry disproportionate bird abundance in the Southwest, so streamflow drives habitat. This edge is what lets every human lever reach wildlife at all.
transfers.evidence: Regression on the project's own annual panel, n = 44 (1980-2024): +0.1953 (t = +2.19, p = 0.029) PDSI-controlled, attenuating to +0.0536 (t = +0.42) with a linear trend added. Positive in both; the conservative estimate ships.
